observations: Photo 0: Side view of a smartphone with a silver or light-colored metallic frame, black front screen, and a visible volume button and mute switch. The phone has a flat edge design, typical of recent iPhone models.

Photo 1: Screen shows 'iPhone Storage' with 256 GB total capacity, 151.97 GB used. The interface is iOS, with a notch at the top. Apps like WhatsApp, Call of Duty, and Snapchat are visible. The time is 6:05, and LTE signal is shown.

Photo 2: Back view of the phone with a white or light gray finish. The camera module has three lenses arranged in a triangular pattern within a square housing, with a flash and sensor. The design matches the iPhone 14 Pro Max or later models, not the iPhone 16 Pro Max, which has a different camera layout and design.

No visible branding or model name on any photo. The seller claims it is an iPhone 16 Pro Max, but the physical design does not match the known design of the iPhone 16 Pro Max (which has a different camera module shape and button layout).

identity.kind: iPhone 14 Pro Max or similar model

claims.evidence: Photo 2 shows a camera module with three lenses in a triangular arrangement within a square housing, which matches the iPhone 14 Pro Max or iPhone 15 Pro Max, not the iPhone 16 Pro Max, which has a different camera layout and design.
Photo 1 clearly shows '151.97 GB of 256 GB used' in the iPhone Storage screen.
No visible proof of origin or activation region. The phone's settings or SIM card information are not shown.

risks.risk: The phone is not an iPhone 16 Pro Max as claimed, but an older model (likely iPhone 14 Pro Max or 15 Pro Max).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the phone's back showing the model name engraved or printed, or a screenshot of the 'Settings > General > About' page showing the model name.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an iPhone 14 Pro Max or similar, not as an iPhone 16 Pro Max, which would be significantly more valuable.

risks.risk: The phone may be locked to a carrier or have activation issues if it is truly from the UK.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the 'Settings > General > About' page showing the model number and carrier lock status, or a video showing the phone being activated with a Nigerian SIM card.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially locked or with activation issues, which reduces value.

risks.risk: Physical damage or wear not visible in photos, such as screen cracks, battery health, or water damage.
risks.proof: A video showing the phone being turned on, used, and rotated to show all sides, including the screen and ports, or a close-up of the battery health in settings.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially damaged or with degraded battery, which reduces value.

proof_requests: Screenshot of 'Settings > General > About' to confirm the exact model name and serial number.
Video showing the phone being turned on, used, and rotated to show all sides, including the screen and ports.
Proof of activation with a Nigerian SIM card or carrier lock status.
